value.rationale: A natural gap remains between the published all-alphabet three-state upper bound and the binary-only two-state classification. The signed graph converts a continuous-parameter lower-bound problem into a small sign/order test on any input word. Its first genuinely ternary failure is fully classified (eight orbits, 48 labeled length-seven suffixes), yielding an explicit regular language of words of maximal state complexity with positive density for any fixed alphabet of at least three symbols. The test is not mere renaming of the binary theorem, and the full cutoff census is mathematical evidence rather than an arbitrary isolated counterexample. The density bound and obstruction are meaningful but not asserted sharp for all hard words.
